steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil lightly greased with cooking spray.
Cut the peeled zucchini in half lengthwise and remove the seeds. Slice the zucchini into 1/2 x 1/2 x 4-inch pieces.

Combine bread crumbs, cheese, and seasoned salt in a deep plate. Dip the zucchini strips into the melted butter, then press into bread crumbs. Gently toss between your hands so any bread crumbs that haven't stuck can fall away. Place the breaded zucchini onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake the zucchini in the preheated oven until the fries are golden and tender, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Crispy Baked Zucchini Fries
raw_recipe.description: This zucchini fries recipe bakes strips of zucchini with Italian seasoned bread crumbs and grated Parmesan cheese until golden, crispy, and very tasty!

review.reviewBody: These were super! In the interest of health I did not use melted butter, but used Olive Oil instead...the coating adhered to the oil and they baked very quickly, with a great flavor. thanks

I adore fried zucchini but don't want the fat from a deep fryer so oven baked is the way to go. I might add that I have fried the zucchini in the past and now that I've tried oven baked I prefer it this way. 

I did modify the recipe slightly. I like the spear shape better, so I cut 2 zucchini in half to make shorter spears (left seeds in since they were not big), then each half was divided into 8 spears. I used 1/3 cup Parmesan cheese and 2/3 cup Panko crumbs (instead of bread crumbs) and I added garlic salt and lemon pepper to taste (didn't measure, just added then tasted to see if I added enough - start with less then you think you need, add more if wanted). I scrambled 2 eggs to dip the zucchini into instead of butter before coating them with my crumbs, but used a little butter to grease my foil since I didn't have any cooking spray. I baked mine for 25 mins (I like them crispy!) @ 425 in a convection toaster oven (didn't even bother turning them) and they came out perfect. I had to bake them in 2 batches because my oven is small. But still this was easier on me than deep frying because you don't have to stand over the stove monitoring the frying process and I was able to get more spears into my oven than I could have fit in a frying pan. Will be doing this again SOON.

These were a huge hit with my entire family. A few tips if you like them super crispy. First, cut the zucchini the shape of thin french fries. Spread zucchini pieces out on a paper towel. Sprinkle with salt and let sit for a while. Then, take another paper towel and blot off all the water. Repeat this step if you have time.

After you've removed as much water as possible, dredge the zucchini pieces in flour, egg, and bread crumbs mixture.

Next, spray a perforated sheet pan or other metal pan that has holes in it with cooking spray. Then, arrange the dredged zucchini in a single layer. Spray a little cooking spray on top of the zucchini. Cook until they begin to brown. Then broil for a few minutes at the end. So crispy and delicious!

Yum. For the first time ever, I used the salt, drain, rinse, and dry method to prep the zucchini to extract excess moisture. It made a Huge difference. I cut the (smallish) zucchini in half and then each half into 8 spears. I used half egg white, half olive oil to coat; then half parm, half panko with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. The spears were small enough to stand them up on the skin side (I always leave the skin on, that's where the good stuff is!) and I didn't have to turn them during cooking, and they only took about fifteen minutes to cook to perfection - ten minutes at 425, and five under the broiler. So delicious. Thank you!

We really liked this but I made a couple of changes. Biggest change is coating everything using ziplock storage bags. Easy and disposable. I coated the zucchini with seasoned flour. The moved it to another ziplock and poured it in the butter. Then I used a spider to move it to seasoned breadcrumb. I seasoned the breadcrumb with garlic powder, salt, pepper, penzey's Tuscan sunset. This would also work well with eggplant
Reading reviews, I used avocado oil to dress the zucchini in before the breadcrumbs. Cooked in a convection oven at 400 degrees and took a few extra minutes to cook, but they were good!

Wonderful and easy to boot! After reading the reviews and seeing the difficulty some people had with the breading, I decided to melt some butter and mix it with olive oil to avoid some of the issues that were mentioned. This worked out very well. I also used whole, unpeeled BABY zucchini and roasted with oiled carrots sticks. Yum! This made a lovely presentation.

I used 2 whole eggs instead of butter. I baked a dozen of unpeeled zucchini sliced round at 425 degrees for 25 minutes, flipping over half way through. I will definitely make this again ! Thanks for sharing.

An excellent recipe! I took the advice of another reviewer and coated them in egg white instead of butter. I cooked them 5 minutes each side at 450, then broiled 2 minutes each side. They came our crispy and delicious!

I did a few things differently. It was faster for me to just slice the zucchini (unpeeled). I also used 2 Tbsp. of milk and 1 egg white mixed together, instead of the butter. Near the end of the cooking time, I set the oven to broil to crisp them up. I also, flipped them once half way through baking. Very good!
Delicious 💯 😋 easy to make. Made these so many times now. Hubby loves them. And he's a very fussy eater
This is a great summer time recipe with zucchini.
Tastes great. A Nice and easy snack or dinner
So good! My husband & I ate the whole pan!
Note that the recipe says to peel the zucchini and the picture shows with peels. I peeled and should not have. It would have turned out better with the peel on.

I recently tried the Crispy Baked Zucchini Fries recipe from Allrecipes, and I was quite impressed! Here's my review: **Pros**: * **Crispy Texture**: The fries had a perfect crispy texture on the outside, thanks to the baking method and the light coating of olive oil and spices. * **Flavor**: The combination of garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and salt added a delicious savory flavor that complemented the natural taste of the zucchini. * **Healthier Option**: Baking the fries instead of frying them makes this recipe a healthier option compared to traditional fried zucchini fries. * **Easy to Make**: The recipe was straightforward and easy to follow, with minimal ingredients and steps. **Cons**: * **Serving Size**: The recipe yielded a smaller number of fries than I expected, so I ended up making a second batch to satisfy my hunger. * **Prep Time**: While the recipe itself is quick, the prep time includes the time it takes to preheat the oven and bake the fries, which can be a bit longer than other recipes. **Overall**: I would highly recommend this recipe for anyone looking for a healthier, yet still delicious, alternative to traditional fried zucchini fries. The crispy texture and savory flavor make them a great snack or side dish. I'll definitely be making these again!

The flavor is good. Tender, yes. Browned and crispy, no. I see that someone else's review for this recipe offers some tips on getting them crispy... it's pretty much a whole different recipe within the review section. :-)
